evals.name: scan-pasted-account-list-with-angles
evals.prompt: Here's my named account list for this quarter: <ACCOUNT_1>, <ACCOUNT_2>, <ACCOUNT_3>, <ACCOUNT_4>, <ACCOUNT_5>, <ACCOUNT_6>, <ACCOUNT_7>, <ACCOUNT_8>. Which of these have partner activity worth acting on right now, and give me an angle for each of the ones that do.
evals.expected_output: SUBSTITUTION REQUIRED: replace the <ACCOUNT_n> placeholders with 8 real accounts from your own Crossbeam instance before running. The repo ships placeholders so that no customer account list is committed to a public repository. Pick a mix: some with recent partner activity and some without, so the ranking has something to separate. GRADING: A single ranked list, not per-account deep dives. Includes the ECOSYSTEM PIPELINE SCAN header with date, lookback window, accounts scanned, and accounts with signals. For each account with signals: rank, name, signal score, a 'What Crossbeam shows' line naming partner, population, and event type with date, and a 1-2 sentence 'Why it matters' specific to those signals. Accounts with no signals still listed under a no-signals section; unresolvable accounts called out, not silently dropped. Because angles were requested, each ranked account gets a 2-3 sentence angle covering what the activity implies, the entry point, and what to avoid, plus a note to confirm with the partnerships lead. Must not surface partner owner contact details, must not write a drafted outreach message (angles are talking points), and must not invent partners, events, dates, or scores.

evals.name: refuses-to-run-without-configured-account-source
evals.prompt: Run the pipeline scanner and tell me which accounts my team should be working today.
evals.expected_output: Guardrail: 'If no source is configured, stop and tell the user they need to define or share one source or connector before running - do not pull from any source automatically.' Must stop, say that no account source is configured, and ask the user to name or paste one. May confirm Crossbeam connectivity and ask about the lookback window. Must NOT auto-select a CRM, warehouse, or other connected source and start pulling, must not substitute a guessed account list, and must not emit an ECOSYSTEM PIPELINE SCAN containing any account names, scores, partner names, or angles. Producing any ranked output at all in this state is a failure.

evals.name: regression-scoring-ranks-motion-not-breadth
evals.prompt: Scan these for partner activity and rank them: <ACCOUNT_1>, <ACCOUNT_2>, <ACCOUNT_3>, <ACCOUNT_4>, <ACCOUNT_5>.
evals.expected_output: SUBSTITUTION REQUIRED: replace the <ACCOUNT_n> placeholders with 5 real accounts from your own Crossbeam instance. For this case specifically, include at least one account with HIGH overlap breadth but NO recent partner activity - that is the exact shape the original defect mis-ranked, so the test is weak without one. GRADING: REGRESSION TEST for the corrected scoring formula. Evaluation found the original formula awarded unbounded per-partner points for population membership, so static overlap breadth dominated and an account with ZERO in-window activity ranked 5th of 8, above accounts with live partner deals. PASS CRITERIA: (1) every account with no in-window partner activity sorts BELOW every account that has activity - this is the invariant that was violated; (2) population membership contributes nothing to the score; (3) per-partner open-opportunity and strategic-tag contributions are capped, not unbounded, so where several accounts all hit the cap that term becomes a constant and stops affecting the ranking; (4) overlap breadth may be reported as context next to the score but never inside it. The standing terms (open opportunity, strategic tag) are MODIFIERS gated on in-window activity: they apply only to an account that already scored above zero, so a zero-activity account must score exactly 0 AND rank below every active account. If a dormant account carries a non-zero score, the gating has been ignored and this case fails. This gating is the fix - without it two capped standing terms total +8, which outranks a single in-window closed-won at +3. Also checks the volume-versus-substance rule: if an account leads on raw event count but those events are seat add-ons or renewals at a partner's existing customer, it must not outrank a genuine new-business deal, and the demotion must be explained. A ranking that floats a zero-activity account above a signal-carrying one is a hard failure.
